recipes.title: Picadillo
recipes.dish_alt: A plate of Cuban picadillo with olives over white rice, served with black beans on a dark plate
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Olives Stirred into the Simmering Picadillo
recipes.prep_alt: A close-up of pimiento-stuffed green olives being stirred into picadillo as it cooks

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Dry white wine or beef stock

sections.heading: Steps
items: Heat the oil in a skillet and sauté the onion and green pepper until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the ground beef, breaking it up with a spoon, and cook until browned.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, wine (or stock), olives, raisins, capers, cumin, oregano, and bay leaf.
Simmer uncovered 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened.
Season with salt and pepper, and remove the bay leaf.
Meanwhile, cook the rice according to package directions.
If using, fry the plantain slices in the oil in a separate pan, 2–3 minutes per side, until golden.
Serve the picadillo over rice with the fried plantains alongside.

recipes.title: Moros y Cristianos with Maduros
recipes.dish_alt: A plate of dark Cuban rice and black beans with fried sweet plantains and roasted pork
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Black Beans and Rice Simmering Together
recipes.prep_alt: A close-up of black beans and rice mixed together for moros y cristianos

sections.heading: Steps
items: Heat the oil in a pot and cook the bacon until it renders its fat and starts to crisp.
Add the onion and green pepper and sauté until soft, then add the garlic and cook 30 seconds.
Stir in the cumin, oregano, and bay leaf.
Add the black beans (with their liquid), rice, and stock. Stir to combine.
Bring to a boil, cover, reduce the heat to low, and simmer 18–20 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Let it rest, covered, 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, remove the bay leaf, and fluff with a fork.
Meanwhile, fry the plantain slices in the oil in a separate pan, 2–3 minutes per side, until golden and caramelized.
Serve the congrí topped with the fried plantains.

recipes.title: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.dish_alt: A round plate of golden yellow rice with a roasted chicken leg and diced red pepper, viewed from above
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Chicken and Rice Simmering in the Pot
recipes.prep_alt: A pot of chicken and yellow rice simmering together with bay leaves

sections.heading: Steps
items: Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large pot or deep skillet, brown the chicken on both sides, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the onion and green pepper until soft, then add the garlic and cook 30 seconds.
Stir in the annatto (or paprika), cumin, and oregano, and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the tomato sauce and wine, if using, and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Add the rice and stir to coat it in the sofrito.
Return the chicken to the pot and pour in the stock. Bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat, and simmer 20–25 minutes until the rice is tender and the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the peas during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Season to taste, garnish with the sliced pimientos, and serve.

recipes.title: Ropa Vieja
recipes.dish_alt: A white plate of shredded beef ropa vieja with yellow rice and black beans
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Shredding the Beef into the Sofrito
recipes.prep_alt: Shredded beef simmering in a tomato-pepper sofrito in a large pan, with a wooden spoon

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Beef stock or water, for boiling

sections.heading: Steps
items: Place the steak, stock (or water), bay leaf, and halved onion in a pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat, cover, and simmer 1–1.5 hours (mostly hands-off) until the meat is fork-tender.
Remove the steak and let it cool slightly, then shred it with two forks along the grain. Reserve 120ml of the cooking liquid; discard the bay leaf and boiled onion.
Heat the oil in a large skillet and sauté the sliced onion and both peppers until soft, about 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in the cumin, oregano, and paprika, and cook 30 seconds more.
Add the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, wine (if using), and the reserved cooking liquid.
Add the shredded beef and olives, and stir to combine.
Simmer uncovered 15–20 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the meat.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot over white rice.

recipes.title: Vaca Frita
recipes.time: 15 min prep + 1–1.5 hr simmer (mostly hands-off) + 10 min fry
recipes.dish_alt: A white plate of crispy pan-fried shredded beef with caramelized onions, served with white rice
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Beef Topped with Onion, Ready to Serve
recipes.prep_alt: Shredded fried beef topped with raw onion rings, served with congrí rice and lettuce

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Beef stock or water, for boiling
Sour orange juice, or extra lime juice

sections.heading: Steps
items: Place the steak, stock (or water), bay leaf, and halved onion in a pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat, cover, and simmer 1–1.5 hours (mostly hands-off) until fork-tender.
Remove the steak, let it cool slightly, then shred it with two forks. Discard the bay leaf and boiled onion.
Toss the shredded beef with the minced garlic, lime juice, sour orange juice, salt, and pepper. Let it marinate 15–20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large skillet until shimmering. Add the beef in a single layer, pressing it down, and fry undisturbed 4–5 minutes until crisp and browned at the edges.
Toss and fry 3–4 minutes more, until well-crisped throughout.
In the same pan (or a separate one), quickly sauté the sliced onion 2–3 minutes until just softened but still with some bite.
Serve the beef topped with the onions and lime wedges.

recipes.title: Caldosa Cubana
recipes.dish_alt: A pot of Cuban caldosa stew with chicken, noodles, potatoes, and carrots in a rich broth
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Caldosa Simmering in the Pot
recipes.prep_alt: Caldosa simmering in a large pot, with noodles, chicken, and root vegetables visible in the broth

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Corn on the cob, cut into chunks

sections.heading: Steps
items: Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the chicken and pork in batches; remove and set aside.
Add the chorizo, onion, and green pepper to the pot and sauté until softened, then add the garlic and cook 30 seconds.
Return the chicken and pork to the pot, add the water (or stock), tomato, cumin, and oregano. Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then reduce the heat, cover, and simmer 40 minutes.
Add the malanga, yuca, and boniato, and simmer 15 minutes more.
Add the calabaza, corn, and plantain, and simmer another 15 minutes until all the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the fideos and cook 5–8 minutes until just tender.
Season with salt and pepper, and finish with a squeeze of lime juice.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot with crusty bread.

recipes.title: Tamales Cubanos
recipes.dish_alt: Two Cuban tamales with their corn husks peeled back, showing the yellow masa filling
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Tamales Wrapped and Tied, Ready to Steam
recipes.prep_alt: Two Cuban tamales wrapped and tied in corn husks, ready to be steamed

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Dried corn husks (or extra strips for tying)
Fresh or frozen corn kernels, pureed
Green bell pepper, finely chopped, for filling

sections.heading: Steps
items: Soak the corn husks in warm water until pliable, about 30 minutes.
Make the filling: heat the oil in a skillet, sauté the onion and green pepper until soft, then add the garlic and cook 30 seconds.
Add the ground pork, breaking it up, and cook until browned. Stir in the tomato sauce, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper. Simmer 5 minutes, then remove from the heat and let cool slightly.
Make the masa: blend the pureed corn, cornmeal, milk, melted butter, sugar, and salt into a thick batter.
Lay a softened corn husk flat, spoon a portion of the masa into the center, and spread it into a rectangle. Add a spoonful of the pork filling down the middle.
Fold the sides of the husk over the filling, then fold the ends up to enclose it, and tie with a strip of husk (or twine).
Repeat with the remaining husks, masa, and filling.
Stand the tamales upright (or lay flat) in a steamer basket over simmering water. Cover and steam 50–75 minutes, until the masa is firm and pulls cleanly from the husk.
Let rest 5 minutes before unwrapping and serving hot.

recipes.title: Flan de Leche (Bonus)
recipes.time: 15 min prep + 35–45 min bake (+ 3 hr chill)
recipes.dish_alt: An unmolded Cuban flan with caramel sauce pooling on a brightly striped plate
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Custard Ready to Serve, Caramel Pooling
recipes.prep_alt: A close-up of caramel custard in a glass bowl with caramel sauce and a spoon

sections.heading: Steps
items: Preheat the oven to 160°C (325°F).

Make the caramel: in a small saucepan, heat the sugar and water over medium heat without stirring until it turns a deep amber, 5–8 minutes. Immediately pour into ramekins (or one baking dish), swirling to coat the bottom.
Whisk the eggs, condensed milk, evaporated milk, vanilla, and salt together until smooth.
Pour the custard over the caramel in the ramekins.
Place the ramekins in a larger baking dish and add hot water to come halfway up their sides (a water bath).
Bake 35–45 minutes, until the custard is just set but still slightly wobbly in the center.
Let cool, then refrigerate at least 3 hours (overnight is best).
Run a knife around the edge and invert onto a plate to unmold, letting the caramel sauce pour over the top.
